description.narrative: The project area is located to the west of Kitui County in Nthongoni location of Kitui Rural sub-county. The name of the project is Muvitha/Kathemboni water shed management aimed at restoration of the catchment which has been degraded over time due poor land use management. Cultivation in steep slopes is evident which would have otherwise been left undisturbed with only trees growing to intercept rainwater and allow it time for water to percolate in the soil and also build up humus. Conservation efforts have been attempted but only when the hills were productive but now signs of neglect have manifested. At the foot of the hills are farms which are still being tilled and whose conservation needs to be strengthened. Within the catchment, there is an earth dam, named Musosya that was constructed in the year 2003 and has silted up due to poor management of land use. During the earth dam construction, there was a perennial flowing stream of water in the main gully that feeds the dam. The situation has since changed and the stream no longer flows and the flow in the gulley’s feeding the dam is only from storm water during the rainy season. Over the years there has been widening of the gully and many more gully tributaries have emerged, gully banks are slumping, widening the stream further and sand accumulation in the main gully has started a sign of mature water course. The silt trap pond that had been made just before the inlet to the dam has been filled with sand, The inlet pat of the dam has also been filled with sand to almost 2m estimated from a tree that was present during the construction of the dam. The tree has been filled by sand to the first branch level. The Water Shed Management project is based on a concept of Land Retention Landscape from Tamera in Portugal that advocates for total retention of storm water run off within a water shed. Tamera consultants have been invited for technical advise with specific deliverable as outlined in the ToR
